name: Salesforce
what: Enterprise CRM for accounts, leads, opportunities, cases, activities, and custom objects.
accessDetail: Developer orgs are self-serve, but useful production credentials and scopes require a Salesforce tenant and administrator.
blocker: Tenant administration, object permissions, security review, and high-risk write actions.

name: HubSpot
what: CRM and marketing platform for contacts, companies, deals, tickets, activities, and content.
accessDetail: Free developer accounts, test accounts, private apps, and OAuth apps are available without sales contact.
blocker: Sensitive-data restrictions, user permissions, rate limits, and confirmation for writes.

name: Pipedrive
what: Sales CRM for deals, leads, people, organizations, activities, products, projects, and webhooks.
accessDetail: A developer sandbox can be requested and API tokens are available in customer accounts.
blocker: No vendor-native MCP verified, but the broad OpenAPI surface is straightforward to wrap.

name: Attio
what: Flexible CRM for people, companies, deals, lists, notes, tasks, meetings, and custom objects.
accessDetail: Developers can create workspaces and API integrations directly.
blocker: Write confirmations, workspace permissions, and bulk-operation guardrails.

name: Twenty
what: Open-source CRM for people, companies, opportunities, activities, workflows, and custom objects.
accessDetail: Self-hosting and cloud workspaces are available, with credentials controlled by the workspace owner.
blocker: Self-hosted version drift, permissions, and destructive write operations.

name: Podio
what: Customizable work platform for apps, items, tasks, contacts, conversations, files, and workflows.
accessDetail: API clients are self-created, but meaningful testing needs a Podio workspace and administrator-approved app access.
blocker: Legacy platform patterns, workspace permissions, and no vendor-native MCP verified.

name: Zoho CRM
what: CRM for leads, contacts, accounts, deals, activities, automation, analytics, and custom modules.
accessDetail: Zoho API Console and trial CRM accounts provide a self-serve credential path.
blocker: Multi-region domains, scopes, edition limits, and confirmation for record mutations.

name: Close
what: Sales CRM for leads, contacts, opportunities, email, calls, SMS, tasks, and reporting.
accessDetail: API keys are generated in a Close account, and a free trial can be used for evaluation.
blocker: Customer communications, calling costs, permissions, and write confirmation.

name: Copper
what: Google Workspace-oriented CRM for people, companies, opportunities, activities, projects, and tasks.
accessDetail: Credentials require a Copper account and administrator access.
blocker: Paid tenant, admin credentials, rate limits, and no vendor-native MCP verified.

name: DealCloud
what: Deal and relationship-management platform for investment and professional-services firms.
accessDetail: API access is tied to a contracted DealCloud tenant and provisioned by administrators or support.
blocker: Enterprise contract, tenant configuration, and no public self-serve sandbox.

name: Zendesk
what: Customer-service platform for tickets, users, organizations, help center, messaging, voice, and routing.
accessDetail: Trials exist, but OAuth clients and production tokens require a Zendesk tenant and admin rights.
blocker: Tenant administration, complex product surfaces, customer-data sensitivity, and no native MCP verified.

name: Intercom
what: Customer support and engagement platform for contacts, conversations, tickets, articles, teams, and messages.
accessDetail: Developer workspaces and apps are self-serve; customer installs use OAuth.
blocker: Workspace permissions, customer-message safety, app review for distribution, and rate limits.

name: Freshdesk
what: Helpdesk for tickets, contacts, agents, companies, groups, solutions, conversations, and time entries.
accessDetail: Free trials and API keys provide a direct testing path.
blocker: No vendor-native MCP verified; normalize product editions and enforce ticket-write guardrails.

name: Front
what: Shared-inbox and customer-operations platform for conversations, messages, contacts, inboxes, tags, and rules.
accessDetail: A Front tenant is needed; OAuth app setup requires administrator configuration.
blocker: OAuth client compatibility, teammate permissions, messaging risk, and beta maturity.

name: Pylon
what: B2B support platform for tickets, customer accounts, Slack and Teams channels, knowledge, and workflows.
accessDetail: API and MCP access require an active Pylon workspace and administrator setup.
blocker: Paid workspace, admin setup, evolving docs, and customer-support data.

name: LiveAgent
what: Helpdesk platform for tickets, chats, calls, contacts, departments, knowledge base, and reports.
accessDetail: A trial account exposes API credentials.
blocker: Versioned endpoints, ticket-write confirmation, and role-based permissions.

name: Plain
what: API-first customer support platform for customers, threads, messages, labels, SLAs, and support workflows.
accessDetail: Developer workspaces and API keys are directly available.
blocker: GraphQL schema complexity, customer-message safety, and tenant permissions.

name: Help Scout
what: Helpdesk for mailboxes, conversations, customers, users, workflows, reports, and knowledge base.
accessDetail: OAuth apps are creatable, but testing needs an active Help Scout account or trial and admin consent.
blocker: Paid tenant, mailbox permissions, communication risk, and no native MCP verified.

name: Gorgias
what: Ecommerce helpdesk for tickets, customers, macros, rules, help center, analytics, and commerce context.
accessDetail: API access requires a Gorgias helpdesk account; the MCP is available on helpdesk plans.
blocker: Beta maturity, role permissions, customer replies, and settings changes.

name: Gladly
what: Enterprise customer-service platform for people, conversations, tasks, channels, knowledge, and routing.
accessDetail: Developer access is associated with an enterprise customer or partner engagement.
blocker: Enterprise contract, provisioned tenant, limited public sandbox access, and no native MCP verified.

name: Slack
what: Team messaging platform for channels, messages, users, files, canvases, workflows, and search.
accessDetail: Apps, development workspaces, tokens, and Socket Mode are self-serve.
apiStyle: REST; Web API; Events; Socket Mode
blocker: Workspace admin policy, granular scopes, message-posting risk, and enterprise controls.

name: Twilio
what: Communications APIs for messaging, voice, verification, phone numbers, video, and email products.
accessDetail: Trial accounts and API credentials are self-serve.
blocker: The official MCP is mainly API-spec and developer tooling; account actions still need explicit API tools and spend controls.

name: Zoho Cliq
what: Team chat platform for channels, messages, users, bots, commands, widgets, and workflows.
accessDetail: Zoho API Console and Cliq workspaces provide a direct path.
blocker: Regional endpoints, workspace permissions, and message-posting confirmation.

name: Lark (Larksuite)
what: Collaboration suite for messaging, calendar, docs, sheets, approvals, contacts, and workplace apps.
accessDetail: Apps are self-created, but production distribution and sensitive permissions require tenant admin or marketplace review.
blocker: Tenant approval, scope review, regional endpoints, and broad cross-product permissions.

name: Pumble
what: Team communication platform for workspaces, channels, messages, users, files, and webhooks.
accessDetail: Workspaces and developer integrations can be created directly.
blocker: Smaller API surface, workspace permissions, and message-write confirmation.

name: Discord
what: Community messaging platform for guilds, channels, messages, members, roles, threads, and interactions.
accessDetail: Developer applications, test servers, bots, and OAuth credentials are self-serve.
blocker: Official MCP is developer documentation context, not a general Discord-account action server; bots still need explicit tools.

name: Telegram
what: Messaging platform with Bot API and client APIs for chats, messages, media, updates, and payments.
accessDetail: BotFather issues bot tokens instantly; full client APIs require an app ID and phone-based account.
blocker: No vendor-native MCP verified, bot limitations, abuse controls, and distinction between Bot API and user accounts.

name: WhatsApp Business
what: Business messaging platform for templates, conversations, media, phone numbers, and webhooks.
authMethods: User token; system-user token; temporary test token
accessDetail: Test numbers are self-serve, while production needs a Meta business, WABA, phone registration, and often verification or review.
blocker: Business verification, template review, messaging policy, phone setup, and customer-consent controls.

name: Aircall
what: Cloud phone and contact-center platform for calls, users, numbers, contacts, tags, and webhooks.
authMethods: OAuth2; Basic with API ID and token
accessDetail: Internal credentials require a customer tenant; public OAuth apps use the Technology Partner path.
blocker: Technology Partner path, tenant access, and no existing Aircall-account MCP; AI Virtual Agent MCP guidance is marked coming soon.

name: Vonage
what: Communications APIs for SMS, voice, video, verification, messaging, and contact-center workflows.
accessDetail: Developer accounts, trial credit, and applications are self-serve.
blocker: Phone-number cost, messaging registration, jurisdictional compliance, and local-tool deployment.

name: Google Ads
what: Advertising API for campaigns, accounts, reporting, audiences, budgets, assets, and conversions.
accessDetail: OAuth is self-serve, but production developer-token access levels are reviewed.
blocker: Developer-token approval, manager-account setup, policy compliance, and read-only MCP scope.

name: Meta Ads
what: Advertising APIs for campaigns, ad sets, creatives, audiences, pixels, insights, and business assets.
accessDetail: Test assets are available, but production permissions often require app review and business verification.
blocker: App review, business verification, asset permissions, and policy-sensitive writes.

name: LinkedIn Ads
what: Marketing APIs for ad accounts, campaigns, creatives, audiences, lead forms, and reporting.
accessDetail: A developer app is self-serve, but Marketing API products and expanded access require application and approval.
blocker: Product-access approval is the main blocker, followed by strict scopes and versioning.

name: GoHighLevel
what: Sales and marketing platform for contacts, conversations, calendars, opportunities, workflows, and agencies.
accessDetail: Private integrations are created inside an account; marketplace apps use OAuth and review.
blocker: Agency or location account, marketplace review, and high-impact workflow actions.

name: Mailchimp
what: Email marketing platform for audiences, campaigns, automations, templates, reports, and ecommerce events.
accessDetail: API keys and OAuth apps are available from a Mailchimp account.
blocker: Vendor MCP coverage is mainly Mailchimp Transactional, not the full Marketing API; enforce consent and sending safeguards.

name: Klaviyo
what: Marketing automation and customer-data platform for profiles, events, lists, segments, campaigns, and metrics.
accessDetail: Private keys are self-serve; public OAuth apps require review and security checks.
blocker: Consent-safe messaging, profile-data sensitivity, OAuth review, and rate limits.

name: systeme.io
what: Funnel, email, course, affiliate, and sales automation platform.
accessDetail: Users can generate public API credentials from their account.
blocker: Narrower surface, email consent, and workflow side effects.

name: Pinterest
what: Visual discovery and advertising platform for pins, boards, catalogs, analytics, and ads.
authMethods: OAuth2 authorization code; client credentials for limited endpoints
accessDetail: Apps need Trial access approval, then Standard access for production breadth and rate limits.
blocker: Trial and Standard review, business account, policy compliance, and no native MCP verified.

name: Threads (Meta)
what: Social publishing API for Threads profiles, posts, replies, mentions, and insights.
accessDetail: Developers can test with app roles; public use follows Meta review and permission rules.
blocker: Meta review, permissions, narrower surface, and no Threads-specific action MCP verified.

name: SendGrid
what: Transactional and marketing email platform for sending, templates, contacts, events, suppressions, and analytics.
accessDetail: Accounts and scoped API keys are self-serve; production sending depends on sender verification.
blocker: Official Twilio MCP and skills expose SendGrid developer context, while execution still needs explicit API tools and reputation controls.

name: Shopify
what: Commerce platform for products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillment, discounts, storefronts, and checkout.
accessDetail: Partner accounts and development stores are self-serve; public distribution uses app review.
apiStyle: GraphQL Admin; Storefront GraphQL; REST legacy; Webhooks
blocker: Admin writes still need GraphQL tools and app scopes; storefront MCP focuses shopping, cart, checkout, and customer tasks.

name: WooCommerce
what: Open-source WordPress commerce platform for products, orders, customers, coupons, shipping, and reports.
authMethods: Consumer key and secret; Basic; OAuth1 over HTTP
accessDetail: Any store owner can install WooCommerce and generate REST credentials.
blocker: WordPress plugin/version variance, self-hosting security, refunds, and destructive store actions.

name: BigCommerce
what: Commerce platform for catalog, orders, customers, inventory, channels, storefronts, carts, and checkout.
accessDetail: Sandbox stores and app credentials are available through the developer portal and trial path.
blocker: Storefront MCP is shopper-focused; admin operations still need scoped API tools and app review.

name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
what: Enterprise commerce platform for products, pricing, inventory, orders, promotions, shoppers, and admin operations.
accessDetail: Requires a contracted Commerce Cloud tenant, API client setup, and administrator-selected roles.
blocker: Enterprise tenant, role configuration, API-family complexity, and Salesforce-hosted MCP setup.

name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
what: Open-source and enterprise commerce platform for catalog, customers, carts, orders, inventory, and extensions.
authMethods: Integration token; OAuth1; OAuth2 server-to-server for SaaS
accessDetail: Magento Open Source is self-hosted; Adobe Commerce cloud features require a paid organization.
blocker: Deployment variation, extension complexity, version drift, and developer-focused rather than universal admin MCP tools.

name: Squarespace
what: Website and commerce platform for products, orders, inventory, transactions, webhooks, and site extensions.
accessDetail: Developers can create apps, but live commerce testing requires a Squarespace site and appropriate plan.
blocker: Paid site, narrower commerce surface, OAuth app setup, and no vendor-native MCP verified.

name: Ecwid
what: Commerce platform for products, orders, customers, inventory, carts, storefront, and app integrations.
accessDetail: Developer apps and test stores are available directly.
blocker: No vendor-native MCP verified; third-party hosted MCP wrappers exist, so provenance and permissions must be reviewed.

name: Gumroad
what: Creator-commerce platform for products, sales, subscribers, licenses, payouts, and resource subscriptions.
accessDetail: Creators can create an OAuth app or access token from their account.
blocker: No official MCP, aging API areas, creator-finance data, and third-party server maintenance.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
what: Marketplace API suite for catalog, listings, orders, inventory, fulfillment, reports, finances, and sellers.
authMethods: Login with Amazon OAuth2; restricted data token
accessDetail: Sandbox onboarding is available, but production developer registration, roles, seller authorization, and security review are substantial.
apiStyle: REST; GraphQL for Data Kiosk; Notifications
blocker: Registration review, restricted-data roles, security controls, seller authorization, and no native MCP verified.

name: fanbasis
what: Creator monetization and commerce platform for offers, payments, communities, and customer operations.
accessDetail: The developer documentation is password-gated and no public self-serve credential path was verified.
blocker: Password-gated docs, unclear auth and surface, and no public sandbox.

name: DataForSEO
what: SEO data APIs for SERPs, keywords, backlinks, domains, business data, app data, and content analysis.
accessDetail: Registration and pay-as-you-go API access are self-serve.
blocker: Usage cost, asynchronous jobs, result size, and no native MCP verified.

name: SE Ranking
what: SEO platform API for rankings, competitors, audits, backlinks, keywords, and projects.
accessDetail: API availability is tied to eligible paid plans and account-issued tokens.
blocker: Paid entitlement, rate limits, job latency, and SEO data cost.

name: Ahrefs
what: SEO and web-intelligence APIs for backlinks, domains, keywords, rankings, and site metrics.
accessDetail: Meaningful API access requires a qualifying paid subscription or API plan.
blocker: Paid entitlement, row-unit cost, quotas, and data licensing.

name: MrScraper
what: Web scraping API for pages, structured extraction, browser rendering, and asynchronous jobs.
accessDetail: Accounts, trial credits, and tokens are self-serve.
blocker: Robots and site terms, dynamic-page reliability, cost, and no native MCP verified.

name: Apify
what: Cloud platform for web-scraping actors, datasets, crawlers, storage, schedules, and automation.
accessDetail: Free accounts, public actors, tokens, and usage credits are self-serve.
blocker: Untrusted actors, scraping legality, spend, long-running jobs, and large datasets.

name: Firecrawl
what: Web crawling and extraction API for scrape, crawl, map, search, structured data, and browser tasks.
accessDetail: Cloud trial credits and open-source self-hosting are available.
blocker: Target-site policy, spend, prompt injection in pages, and asynchronous crawling.

name: Bright Data
what: Web data platform for proxies, scraping browser, datasets, SERP, unlocker, and crawlers.
accessDetail: Trials exist, but production requires paid zones, compliance checks, and configured products.
blocker: Compliance, proxy spend, target-site policy, sensitive datasets, and administrator controls.

name: Sherlock
what: Open-source CLI that checks usernames across many social networks.
accessDetail: Source and package are public and run locally.
blocker: False positives, site changes, rate limits, privacy, and misuse prevention.

name: Waterfall.io
what: Contact and company intelligence platform for enrichment, identity resolution, and multi-provider data waterfalls.
accessDetail: API access requires a paid workspace or sales-assisted plan.
blocker: Paid credits, personal-data handling, provider provenance, and no native MCP verified.

name: Clay
what: GTM data and workflow platform for enrichment, research, tables, signals, sequencing, and provider orchestration.
accessDetail: Workspace and API access depend on plan and administrator settings; new accounts receive limited credits.
blocker: Credit burn, provider terms, admin controls, personal data, and workflow side effects.

name: GitHub
what: Code-hosting platform for repositories, issues, pull requests, actions, releases, projects, and security.
accessDetail: Accounts, apps, test repositories, and scoped tokens are self-serve.
blocker: Repository permissions, destructive actions, branch protection, secrets, and prompt-injection risk.

name: Vercel
what: Cloud platform for projects, deployments, domains, environment variables, logs, analytics, and teams.
accessDetail: Free accounts, teams, projects, and personal tokens are self-serve.
blocker: Deployment, domain, environment-secret, and production mutation safeguards.

name: Netlify
what: Cloud platform for sites, deploys, functions, forms, domains, environment variables, and teams.
accessDetail: Free accounts and personal tokens are self-serve.
blocker: Production deploys, secrets, domains, and team permissions.

name: Cloudflare
what: Internet platform for DNS, zones, Workers, storage, security, analytics, tunnels, and accounts.
accessDetail: Free accounts and scoped API tokens are self-serve.
blocker: Massive surface, DNS and security blast radius, account scopes, and write confirmation.

name: Supabase
what: Backend platform for Postgres, auth, storage, edge functions, realtime, projects, and management.
authMethods: Project API key; personal access token; database credentials
accessDetail: Free projects and credentials are self-serve.
blocker: Database writes, service-role keys, production-project targeting, and schema migration risk.

name: Neo4j
what: Graph database platform for Cypher queries, graph data, schemas, instances, and analytics.
accessDetail: Aura free instances and local Community Edition are self-serve.
blocker: Arbitrary Cypher, data mutation, query cost, and credential scoping.

name: Snowflake
what: Cloud data platform for warehouses, databases, SQL, data sharing, apps, governance, and AI services.
authMethods: OAuth2; key-pair JWT; programmatic access token
accessDetail: Trials exist, but useful access requires an account, roles, warehouses, and administrator policies.
blocker: Role design, warehouse cost, sensitive data, arbitrary SQL, and administrator setup.

name: MongoDB Atlas
what: Managed database platform for clusters, projects, users, backups, alerts, search, and data operations.
authMethods: Service-account OAuth2; public/private API key; database user
accessDetail: Free Atlas projects and credentials are self-serve.
blocker: Database mutation, project admin actions, network access lists, and production targeting.

name: Datadog
what: Observability platform for metrics, logs, traces, monitors, incidents, dashboards, SLOs, and security.
authMethods: API key and app key; OAuth2
accessDetail: Trials exist; API and app keys are created inside an organization with role permissions.
blocker: Sensitive telemetry, monitor mutations, incident actions, and organization-level permissions.

name: Sentry
what: Error and performance platform for issues, events, releases, projects, alerts, traces, and organizations.
accessDetail: Free organizations, developer apps, and scoped tokens are self-serve.
blocker: Issue mutations, release actions, sensitive stack data, and organization permissions.

name: Notion
what: Workspace platform for pages, databases, data sources, blocks, users, comments, and search.
accessDetail: Free workspaces and internal integrations are self-serve; public apps use OAuth review.
blocker: Page sharing, user permissions, destructive edits, and rich block structure.

name: Airtable
what: Low-code data platform for bases, tables, records, fields, comments, webhooks, and automations.
accessDetail: Free bases, PATs, and OAuth apps are self-serve.
blocker: Schema variability, record writes, base permissions, and rate limits.

name: Linear
what: Issue and product-development platform for teams, projects, cycles, issues, comments, documents, and roadmaps.
accessDetail: Free workspaces, personal keys, and OAuth apps are self-serve.
blocker: Workspace permissions, issue mutation, notification noise, and automation loops.

name: Jira
what: Issue and project platform for work items, projects, comments, users, boards, sprints, and workflows.
accessDetail: Free Jira sites, developer apps, and OAuth are self-serve; enterprise admins can restrict apps.
blocker: Complex permissions, workflow transitions, enterprise app policy, and bulk edits.

name: Asana
what: Work-management platform for tasks, projects, portfolios, goals, teams, users, and attachments.
accessDetail: Developer apps, PATs, and free workspaces are self-serve.
blocker: Task mutation, team permissions, notification noise, and rate limits.

name: Monday.com
what: Work operating system for boards, items, columns, updates, users, workspaces, and automations.
accessDetail: Developer apps and trial accounts provide a self-serve path.
blocker: Highly dynamic schemas, complexity quotas, board permissions, and write confirmation.

name: ClickUp
what: Productivity platform for workspaces, spaces, folders, lists, tasks, comments, docs, goals, and time.
accessDetail: Free workspaces, personal tokens, and OAuth apps are self-serve.
blocker: Hierarchy complexity, permissions, task mutation, and rate limits.

name: Coda
what: Collaborative document platform for docs, pages, tables, rows, formulas, controls, and automations.
accessDetail: Free docs, API tokens, and OAuth apps are self-serve.
blocker: Document sharing, formula side effects, row mutations, and sync-table semantics.

name: Smartsheet
what: Enterprise work-management platform for sheets, rows, reports, dashboards, attachments, and automation.
accessDetail: API access requires a Smartsheet account; enterprise administrators may restrict integrations.
blocker: Paid tenant, admin policy, spreadsheet-like schema variability, and no native MCP verified.

name: Harvest
what: Time tracking and invoicing platform for time entries, projects, clients, users, expenses, and invoices.
accessDetail: Trials, personal tokens, and OAuth apps are self-serve.
blocker: No native MCP verified; enforce time-entry and invoice write confirmation.

name: Stripe
what: Payments platform for customers, payments, subscriptions, invoices, products, disputes, and connected accounts.
authMethods: Secret API key; restricted key; OAuth2
accessDetail: Test mode, accounts, keys, and Connect apps are self-serve.
blocker: Money movement, refunds, disputes, PCI boundaries, test-versus-live mode, and idempotency.

name: Plaid
what: Financial-data platform for bank linking, accounts, transactions, identity, assets, risk, and payments.
authMethods: Client ID and secret; OAuth2 for Dashboard MCP
accessDetail: Sandbox is self-serve, but live data and products require Production approval and compliance review.
blocker: Production approval, financial data, product eligibility, and MCP scope focused on diagnostics and sandbox tooling.

name: Binance
what: Crypto exchange APIs for market data, account data, orders, wallets, transfers, and trading.
authMethods: API key; HMAC or asymmetric signature
accessDetail: Accounts and API keys are self-serve where the service is legally available; trading and withdrawals require KYC and controls.
blocker: Jurisdiction, KYC, trading loss, withdrawal risk, rate limits, and key restrictions.

name: Paygent Connect
what: NMI-powered payment connectivity for merchant processing and payment workflows.
accessDetail: No clear public developer credential path or sandbox specific to Paygent Connect was verified.
blocker: Ambiguous product identity, NMI dependency, partner provisioning, and sparse public docs.

name: iPayX
what: AI-oriented payments and financial operations platform with documented API and MCP access.
accessDetail: Credentials and production use appear tied to an approved customer workspace or paid account.
blocker: Young documentation footprint, financial controls, customer eligibility, and money movement.

name: QuickBooks
what: Accounting platform for companies, customers, invoices, bills, payments, reports, and bookkeeping data.
accessDetail: Developer accounts and sandbox companies are self-serve; production applications may require Intuit review.
blocker: Production review, accounting correctness, tenant authorization, sensitive data, and no native MCP verified.

name: Xero
what: Cloud accounting platform for organizations, invoices, contacts, bank transactions, payroll, projects, and reports.
accessDetail: Apps and trials are self-serve; public production use follows consent, certification, and partner rules.
blocker: Accounting sensitivity, tenant consent, certification, and region-specific payroll.

name: Brex
what: Business finance platform for cards, expenses, reimbursements, travel, budgets, users, and payments.
accessDetail: API access is tied to a Brex customer account, administrator authorization, or approved partner integration.
blocker: Customer eligibility, admin approval, finance controls, and high-risk card or payment actions.

name: Ramp
what: Corporate finance platform for cards, expenses, reimbursements, bills, travel, users, and accounting.
accessDetail: Developers need a Ramp customer or partner account, and administrators authorize apps and scopes.
blocker: Customer account, admin approval, sensitive financial data, and money-moving operations.

name: PitchBook
what: Private-market research platform for companies, deals, investors, funds, people, and market intelligence.
accessDetail: API and direct-data access are enterprise products sold through PitchBook.
blocker: Enterprise contract, licensing, redistribution limits, and no self-serve sandbox.

name: NotebookLM
what: AI research workspace grounded in uploaded sources, notebooks, audio, and enterprise knowledge.
authMethods: Google OAuth2; Application Default Credentials; service account
accessDetail: The programmable NotebookLM Enterprise API is part of Gemini Enterprise and needs a Cloud project, billing, and admin configuration.
blocker: Enterprise access, v1alpha stability, admin setup, source governance, and no standalone MCP verified.

name: Otter AI
what: Meeting transcription platform for recordings, transcripts, summaries, action items, and chat.
accessDetail: Otter states it has no general public REST API; official MCP and custom app setup depend on plan and support.
blocker: No public REST API, plan eligibility, support-gated setup, and sensitive meeting data.

name: Fathom
what: AI meeting assistant for recordings, transcripts, summaries, action items, CRM sync, and team insights.
accessDetail: Users can generate an API key in settings; OAuth registration is available for multi-user integrations, and the official MCP uses OAuth.
blocker: Meeting privacy, participant consent, workspace permissions, and transcript retention.

name: Consensus
what: AI academic-search product for finding, synthesizing, and citing peer-reviewed research.
authMethods: OAuth2 through MCP; issued API access
accessDetail: The official MCP is directly connectable. It works without an account at low limits, with higher limits after free OAuth sign-in; separate API access is request-based.
blocker: Low free-tier quotas, citation fidelity, query pacing, and product-specific corpus coverage.

name: Reducto
what: Document ingestion and parsing platform for OCR, layout, tables, extraction, splitting, and structured output.
authMethods: API key; OAuth device flow for MCP
accessDetail: Developers can sign up, obtain trial credits, and use the API directly.
blocker: Document privacy, large files, asynchronous jobs, extraction uncertainty, and credit controls.

name: Devin
what: Autonomous software-engineering agent platform for coding sessions, repositories, tasks, knowledge, and automation.
accessDetail: API and MCP require a Devin organization and administrator-issued service-user credentials.
blocker: Paid organization, repository permissions, cost, and autonomous code-change risk.

name: Higgsfield
what: Generative media suite and CLI for creating, editing, and orchestrating video, images, and content workflows.
accessDetail: Users can create an account and install the CLI or MCP integration; generation depends on credits.
blocker: Credit spend, asynchronous generation, media-safety policy, and large artifacts.

name: Mermaid CLI
what: Open-source command-line renderer that converts Mermaid diagrams into SVG, PNG, or PDF.
accessDetail: The package and source are public and run locally.
blocker: Untrusted diagram input, Chromium sandboxing, file paths, and resource limits.

name: YouTube Transcript
what: Third-party API for YouTube transcripts, channel data, search results, and transcript workflows.
accessDetail: Developers can sign up for trial credits and an API key.
blocker: Third-party dependency, unavailable captions, YouTube policy, rate limits, and content rights.

name: Grain
what: AI meeting-notes platform for recordings, transcripts, summaries, clips, stories, and CRM workflows.
accessDetail: The official MCP works across Free, Starter, Business, and Enterprise plans; deal and coaching tools require higher plans.
blocker: Workspace authorization, meeting privacy, participant consent, and premium-only deal or coaching tools.
